title: PM to Visit Gujarat on 30-31 October
subtitle:
PM to Lay the Foundation Stone, Inaugurate and Dedicate to the Nation Development Projects Worth Over ₹14,000 Crore in Banaskantha

PM to Release 24th Instalment of PM-KISAN, Amounting to Around ₹19,000 Crore

PM to Dedicate Bharat Bovine Breeding and Research Centre in Banaskantha

PM to Lay the Foundation Stone of Ahmedabad Metro Phase-2A (Airport Extension) and Phase-2B (GIFT City Extension)

PM to Inaugurate Bharat Parv 2026 and Witness Ekta Prakash Parv at Ekta Nagar

PM to Participate in Rashtriya Ekta Diwas Celebrations Marking the 151st Birth Anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel

This Year’s Parade to Place Special Emphasis on Achievements of Security Forces in Combating Left-Wing Extremism

‘Vande Mataram’ to Be the Overarching Theme of Rashtriya Ekta Diwas Celebrations

PM to Inaugurate and Lay the Foundation Stone for Development Projects Worth Over ₹400 Crore in Ekta Nagar
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 OCT 2026 2:56PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will visit Gujarat on 30-31 October 2026.
On 30 October, at around 9:30 AM, the Prime Minister will visit the Embryo Transfer Technology-In Vitro Fertilisation (ET-IVF) Laboratory and the Bharat Bovine Breeding and Research Centre (BBBRC) cattle farm in Banaskantha. At around 10:30 AM, he will lay the foundation stone, inaugurate and dedicate to the nation various development projects worth over ₹14,000 crore in Banaskantha. He will also release the 24th instalment under PM-KISAN, amounting to ₹19,000 crore, flag off two train services and address the gathering on the occasion.
Thereafter, Prime Minister will travel to Ekta Nagar, Kevadia. At around 5 PM, he will inaugurate Bharat Parv 2026. At around 7:45 PM, he will witness Ekta Prakash Parv, followed by Narmada Aarti at around 8:15 PM.
On 31 October, at around 9 AM, Prime Minister will offer floral tributes at the Statue of Unity. Thereafter, at around 9:15 AM, he will lay the foundation stone, inaugurate and dedicate to the nation various development projects worth over ₹400 crore in Ekta Nagar. He will subsequently visit the Rain Forest and Vaman Vriksha Vatika in Ekta Nagar. At around 5:30 PM, Prime Minister will participate in the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebrations commemorating the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
PM in Banaskantha
Prime Minister will dedicate to the nation the Bharat Bovine Breeding and Research Centre (BBBRC) at Bhildi in Banaskantha, Gujarat. Spread over 127 acres, it has been established as a state-of-the-art Centre of Excellence. The BBBRC will strengthen bovine breeding, genetic upgradation and advanced reproductive technologies, accelerating breed improvement by 10–20 times. It will be the country’s first facility of its kind dedicated to the Kankrej cattle breed.
Prime Minister will lay the foundation stones for two Bio-CNG plants of Banas Dairy at Tharad and Radhanpur, with cattle dung processing capacities of 75 metric tonnes per day and 100 metric tonnes per day, respectively.
Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone of Ahmedabad Metro Phase-2A (Airport Extension) and Phase-2B (GIFT City Extension). Phase-2A will have a length of over 6 km, covering five stations from Koteshwar Road to the Airport, while Phase-2B will have a length of over 3.3 km, covering three stations from GIFT City to Shahpur.
Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone for the upgradation and strengthening of the Ahmedabad-Mehsana Road (State Highway-41) from four lanes to eight lanes, at a cost of around ₹2,600 crore. The project will make travel between Ahmedabad and North Gujarat faster, safer and more comfortable.
Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone for 4,030 new child-friendly Anganwadi Centres and inaugurate 361 completed child-friendly Anganwadi Centres in Gujarat. With an investment of ₹800 crore, the initiative will benefit more than 4 lakh people.
Prime Minister will dedicate to the nation 521 projects completed under the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund, involving a total project cost of around ₹4,950 crore. These projects include cold storage facilities and cold chains, warehouses, silos, polyhouses and greenhouses, integrated primary and secondary processing facilities, and primary processing centres.
Prime Minister will inaugurate the expansion of the potato processing plant at Sanadar and commission the Automated Storage and Retrieval System (ASRS) for ultra-high-temperature (UHT) products at Palanpur.
Prime Minister will flag off the Ahmedabad (Sabarmati)-Varanasi Express and the Mehsana-Becharaji-Sabarmati MEMU train services, strengthening rail connectivity.
Prime Minister will release the 24th instalment of PM-KISAN, amounting to ₹19,000 crore, providing continued financial assistance to farmers across the country. He will also mark the commencement of on-ground activities under 12 approved horticulture clusters. Covering approximately 1.46 lakh hectares, these clusters are expected to benefit over 1.3 lakh farmers. Two clusters in North Gujarat will focus on potatoes.
PM in Ekta Nagar
On 30 October, as part of the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebrations, Prime Minister will inaugurate Bharat Parv 2026 at Ekta Nagar. Conceived as a celebration of India’s cultural heritage and national unity and symbolizing the spirit of Ek Bharat Shreshth Bharat, the festival will provide a platform for States and Union Territories to showcase their distinctive traditions, folk performances, regional cuisines, handicrafts and tourist attractions. The festival is expected to boost tourism in Ekta Nagar and surrounding destinations. It will continue until 15 November 2026.
Prime Minister will witness Ekta Prakash Parv, a festival of illumination celebrating India’s unity, diversity, cultural heritage and progress. The festival promotes night tourism in Ekta Nagar through thematic illumination and lighting displays. It has two major attractions. The 530-metre-long Valley of Flowers Road illumination, themed ‘From Ancient India to Modern India’, showcases India’s national identity, civilisation, women’s empowerment, security forces, technology, yoga and an imaginative world for children. The 180-metre-long Glow Tunnel, themed “Unity in India’s Diversity”, offers a walkthrough experience of the cultures, architecture, folk dances, handicrafts and lifestyles of India’s four regions. Over 1.5 crore LED lights have been used in the displays, with artworks created by artists from different parts of the country.
On 31 October, Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone, inaugurate and dedicate to the nation various development projects worth over ₹400 crore in Ekta Nagar. The projects to be inaugurated include a sewage and water treatment plant, facade lighting, the upgradation of Narmada Ghat, an IRCTC hotel, and the Rainforest, Unity and Eco Trail at Ekta Nagar, among others. Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone of various projects including Gora-Bhandra Road Development; integrated zero waste smart solid waste management project; Khalwani Eco Tourism Development; Integrated Development at Cactus & Butterfly Garden among others.
Prime Minister will participate in Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebrations on 31 October 2026, commemorating the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
Ekta Parade will showcase the discipline, professionalism, courage and dedication of the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs), State Police Forces and Central Police Organisations. This year’s parade will place special emphasis on the achievements of security forces in combating Left-Wing Extremism and the transformation of previously affected areas towards peace, security and development.
A major highlight of the celebrations will be a special theatrical presentation on Naxal Mukt Bharat, organised by the National School of Drama (NSD), featuring approximately 2,000 artists from 126 districts affected by Left-Wing Extremism. Through theatrical performances, the artists will portray the challenges faced by communities in these regions and their journey towards peace, security and development.
The tableaux and cultural performances will be centred on Vande Mataram, reflecting patriotism, national pride and collective belonging. The tableaux will showcase the aspirations of people, the cultural richness of States and Union Territories, and the development journeys of people.
A grand cultural presentation featuring approximately 5,000 artists from across India will celebrate the country’s diverse classical and folk traditions, music, dance and artistic heritage.

title: AIIA-iCAINE Marks Sixth Foundation Day with Launch of National Ayurveda AI Challenge in Collaboration with Techfest, IIT Bombay
subtitle:
Two MoUs Signed to Strengthen Ayurveda Innovation and Industry–Academia Collaboration; IPR Facility for Ayurveda Launched

Incubator Has Supported 52 Problem Statements, Mentored Over 100 Startup Ideas and Provided Seed Support of ₹3 Lakh Each to Nine Startups
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 OCT 2026 7:18PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi, celebrated the sixth Foundation Day of its incubation centre, AIIA-iCAINE, with the launch of a national innovation challenge in Artificial Intelligence (AI) for Ayurveda, the signing of two strategic Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs), the launch of an Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) Facility for Ayurveda and a capacity-building workshop on entrepreneurship and design thinking.
On the occasion, Prof. Vd. P. K. Prajapati, Director, AIIA, highlighted the incubator’s continued efforts to promote innovation, strengthen industry–academia collaboration and translate Ayurvedic knowledge and research into practical solutions, products and enterprises.
“Over the past six years, AIIA-iCAINE has undertaken several initiatives to promote innovation and entrepreneurship in Ayurveda. The incubator has supported 52 problem statements and mentored more than 100 startup ideas. Furthermore, nine startups have received seed support of ₹3 lakh each, helping them advance their entrepreneurial journeys,” he said.
The highlight of the celebration was the launch of AyushTech Innovate: National Open Ayurveda AI Challenge, organised by Techfest, IIT Bombay, in collaboration with the Ministry of Ayush and AIIA.
Leveraging AyurParam, IIT Bombay’s open-source Ayurveda Large Language Model, the challenge aims to encourage the development of trustworthy, transparent, safe and practical AI solutions for Ayurveda. It will address challenges in Ayurvedic clinical practice, classical text retrieval, research, treatment planning and public health awareness.
The national grand finale is scheduled to take place at IIT Bombay from December 15 to 18, 2026.
AIIA-iCAINE signed two strategic MoUs to strengthen research, innovation and commercialisation in Ayurveda.
The MoU with the World Ayurveda Foundation (WAF) will facilitate the establishment of “AI in Ay – Secretariat for Artificial Intelligence in Ayurveda”, a collaborative platform to advance AI-driven research, innovation and entrepreneurship. The collaboration will support joint research, funding and CSR proposals, capacity-building programmes, hackathons and startup incubation. It will also leverage WAF’s national and international networks to promote responsible AI applications in Ayurveda.
The MoU with Reliance Retail Limited (Pahadi Local) will facilitate the translation of classical Ayurvedic knowledge into commercially viable skincare products through formulation advisory. Reliance Retail will undertake product development, testing, manufacturing and marketing, creating a pathway for the commercialisation of Ayurveda-based innovations and strengthening industry–academia collaboration.
Another key development was the launch of the Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) Facility for Ayurveda, aimed at promoting awareness of intellectual property protection and helping Ayurveda innovators and entrepreneurs understand the importance of safeguarding their innovations as they progress towards product development and commercialisation.
The Foundation Day activities also included a capacity-building workshop on branding, pricing strategies and design thinking for Ayurveda ventures.
Ms Jessica of Reliance Retail Limited conducted the masterclass on branding, while Sujith Eranezhath, CEO, AIIA-iCAINE, led the session on pricing strategies and the design-thinking masterclass. The sessions covered user needs assessment, problem identification, ideation, prototyping, testing and the development of practical, user-centred solutions for the Ayurveda sector.
Other highlights included a briefing on the Smart India Hackathon (SIH), the launch of the Techfest Hackathon, the release of Ayupreneur: A Beginner’s Glossary and the release of grants to the SIH 2025 winners.
The official programme began with a welcome address by Dr Arun Kumar Mahaptra, Head of Incubation. The programme featured an address by Prof. (Dr.) Sreenivasa Prasad Buduru, Chief Guest, and the presidential address by Prof. Vd. P. K. Prajapati, Director, AIIA.
The celebration concluded with a vote of thanks by Sujith Eranezhath, CEO, AIIA-iCAINE, followed by networking.
About AIIA-iCAINE
Established on October 29, 2021, under the mandate of the Ministry of Ayush, Government of India, AIIA-iCAINE is recognised as India’s first public-sector Ayurveda business incubator. It works to promote innovation, startup incubation and entrepreneurship by supporting the development of Ayurveda-based products, services and enterprises through mentorship, capacity building, institutional partnerships and industry engagement.

title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi to Release 24th Instalment of PM-KISAN tomorrow  at Banaskantha, Gujarat
subtitle:
Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan to participate in the programme to mark the release at Raisen, Madhya Pradesh

Over 9.34 crore farmers to receive more than ₹18,690 crore through Direct Benefit Transfer

Dedication of 521 units developed under Agriculture Infrastructure Fund to the nation to strengthen agricultural storage, processing and related infrastructure

Inaugaration of 12 Horticulture Clusters to promote high-value horticultural crops and enhance the income potential of farmers

The initiatives will further the Government’s efforts to build a prosperous, resilient and self-reliant agricultural sector in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 OCT 2026 6:46PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will release the 24th instalment of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) tomorrow (30 October 2026) at Banaskantha, Gujarat. The instalment will transfer more than ₹18,690 crore directly to the bank accounts of over 9.34 crore farmers across the country, which focuses the Government’s commitment towards the welfare and economic empowerment of farmers.
The Prime Minister will also dedicate to the nation 521 units established under the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund to strengthen agricultural storage, processing and related infrastructure, and inaugurate 12 horticulture clusters to promote high-value horticultural crops and enhance the income potential of farmers.
Union Minister of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan will participate in the programme to mark the release of the 24th instalment of PM-KISAN at Raisen, Madhya Pradesh. The event is expected to witness the participation of a large number of farmers from the region, providing an important platform to highlight the significance of PM-KISAN and other key initiatives of the Department, while reaffirming the Government’s continued commitment to farmers’ welfare, prosperity and empowerment.
Through the first 23 instalments of PM-KISAN, more than ₹4.47 lakh crore has already been disbursed to eligible farmers. The scheme provides income support to eligible farmer families through Direct Benefit Transfer, helping them meet agricultural and household expenses and supporting their livelihood security.
Agriculture is the backbone of India’s economy, supporting the livelihoods of crores of farmers and ensuring the food and nutritional security. Under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Government has undertaken several significant initiatives over the past 12 years to improve farmers’ incomes, promote modern agricultural practices aming to achieve the goal and vision of self-reliance in agriculture sector.
Key initiatives include the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN), Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana, Kisan Credit Card, Minimum Support Price (MSP),
Per Drop More Crop
. These measures aim to provide financial assistance, strengthen risk protection, improve access to agricultural credit and promote technology-driven agricultural governance for holistic empowerment of farmers.
The Government is also advancing self-reliance in agriculture through initiatives such as the National Mission on Edible Oils and the Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses. In addition, the National Mission on Natural Farming is encouraging farmers to adopt sustainable agricultural practices through the development of clusters across the country.
Recognising the importance of post-harvest management and agricultural infrastructure in improving farmers’ returns, the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) promotes investments in warehouses, cold storage facilities, primary processing centres and other essential agricultural infrastructure. Under the AIF, investments of approximately ₹1.75 lakh crore have been made across more than 2.28 lakh projects, supporting the development of critical agricultural infrastructure across the country. These investments are expected to strengthen storage and processing capabilities, reduce post-harvest losses, improve market access and enable farmers to obtain better returns for their produce.
The Government is also promoting diversification towards high-value agricultural activities, particularly horticulture, to enhance income opportunities and make farming more remunerative. The development of horticulture clusters is an important step towards strengthening the horticulture value chain and encouraging the production and marketing of high-value crops.
These initiatives will further the Government’s efforts to provide financial support to farmers, modernise agricultural infrastructure, promote crop diversification and build a prosperous, resilient and self-reliant agricultural sector in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat.

title: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry, Shri Piyush Goyal Calls for Greater FTA Utilisation by Telangana
subtitle:
Shri Piyush Goyal Calls for Pharma Innovation, Global GI Exports and Ease of Doing Business to Drive Telangana’s Growth

India’s FTAs Provide Preferential Market Access to 76% of Global GDP: Shri Piyush Goyal
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 OCT 2026 9:47PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry, Shri Piyush Goyal, today highlighted India’s growing trade partnerships, policy stability and investment opportunities while addressing the curtain raiser of the Invest Telangana Global Summit in New Delhi. Congratulating the Chief Minister of Telangana, Shri A. Revanth Reddy, on convening the summit, Shri Goyal said the State’s ambition to become a $3 trillion economy by 2047 was achievable through collective efforts by the Central Government, State Government, industry, investors and citizens.
Shri Goyal said India’s existing trade agreements had provided preferential market access to a global GDP of $70 trillion, including $10 trillion through agreements finalised more than a decade ago and an additional $60 trillion through the nine recently finalised agreements. With negotiations underway for another eight bilateral or multilateral agreements, which he said would add a further $15 trillion, India would have preferential market access covering approximately 76 per cent of the global GDP of $115 trillion.
He noted that the IMF had projected global trade growth of barely 1.9 per cent amid global challenges. Against this backdrop, India set a target of $1 trillion in exports, aiming for 15 per cent growth in the current year. He said the target reflected the collective conviction of exporters, industry associations and businesses to surpass conventional forecasts.
Highlighting India’s economic performance, Shri Goyal said the country had moved from the “Fragile Five” a decade ago to the world’s fifth-largest economy and the fastest-growing large economy. He cited growth of 7.7 per cent in the previous year and 7.8 per cent in the first quarter of the current year, expressing the expectation that growth would remain above 7 per cent in the quarter ending September. He also referred to the IMF’s recent assessment of stronger-than-expected economic performance and its expectation that India would continue to be the fastest-growing large economy in the current and following year.
The Minister acknowledged global uncertainties arising from conflicts in West Asia and Ukraine and disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz. He said India continued to demonstrate resilience amid these challenges and highlighted upgrades to India’s credit rating by multiple international rating agencies, including the Japanese Credit Rating Agency (JCR), which upgraded India’s rating for the first time in over 35 years.
The Minister said India offered investors stable policies, open borders, supply chain resilience and the assurance that the rule of law would protect their interests. He highlighted that, over the preceding four and a half years, India had negotiated and finalised nine free trade agreements or bilateral trade agreements, opening opportunities for Indian businesses in 38 developed countries. He said these countries offered complementary capabilities, including advanced equipment, modern technologies, high-tech devices and graphics processing units (GPUs) required by Indian industry.
Referring to Telangana’s historical trading traditions, Shri Goyal recalled the Motupalli Abhaya Shasana, a maritime charter issued in 1244 by Kakatiya ruler, Ganapati Deva, which promoted stability and predictability in trade. He drew parallels with the present, noting that investors continue to seek certainty and continuity in policy.
Emphasising the collective responsibility towards Viksit Bharat 2047, Shri Goyal said the country’s journey towards shared prosperity required the collective drive and energy of 1.4 billion Indians. He said the commitment and capabilities of Telangana’s skilled, qualified and youthful population could help the State set new benchmarks for growth and development.
Referring to Telangana’s aspiration to grow from an economy of approximately $200 billion to $3 trillion by 2047, he welcomed the target set by the state government.
“Impossible doesn’t exist in my dictionary,” Shri Goyal said, acknowledging that achieving the target would require considerable collective effort. He said the Central Government, State Government, businesses, investors, farmers, fishermen, technical manpower, scientists, innovators, startups, women entrepreneurs and officials would all have to contribute to the State’s development.
Shri Goyal said Telangana is well positioned to contribute to the Viksit Bharat vision through its pharmaceutical industry, aerospace and defence capabilities, value-added agriculture, food processing, research and development, innovation and services sector. He also highlighted the opportunities presented by global capability centres, design and innovation, and the State’s talent in artificial intelligence and quantum computing.
Emphasising that every contribution mattered to economic development, the Minister referred to the dispatch of 2.5 metric tonnes of GI-tagged Tandur red gram from Hyderabad to Australia, leveraging the India-Australia free trade agreement. He said such exports demonstrated how trade agreements could create opportunities not only for large industries but also for farmers and smaller producers.
Shri Goyal emphasised that every contribution, big or small, was important to India’s development journey. He highlighted the role of farmers, entrepreneurs, MSMEs and other stakeholders in collectively advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.
The Minister reiterated the Central Government’s commitment to Telangana’s development and referred to projects launched or supported in the State. He mentioned the foundation stone for the Zaheerabad Industrial Smart City, which he said would provide plug-and-play industrial land for automobiles, food processing, machinery and electrical equipment. He also referred to the Kakatiya Mega Textile Park in Warangal, describing it as the first fully functional PM MITRA park, and highlighted its alignment with the 5F vision of “farm to fibre, fibre to factory, factory to fashion, and fashion to foreign”.
Calling for closer coordination between the Centre and the States, Shri Goyal said Telangana’s development vision for 2047 was aligned with the national vision of Viksit Bharat articulated by Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi.
Outlining six suggestions for the way forward, Shri Goyal proposed that Telangana identify its 50 leading export products across goods and services and map markets offering preferential access under existing FTAs. He also suggested setting up FTA help desks in every district to help MSMEs, farmers and startups make the most of these agreements.
He called for taking GI-tagged products such as Tandur red gram, Chatpata chilli and Nizamabad turmeric to global markets, stressing the need for traceability, packaging and branding to help farmers secure a premium for their produce.
Shri Goyal suggested moving Telangana’s pharmaceutical industry up the value chain by strengthening domestic capabilities in key starting materials and active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), investing in innovation, and moving beyond generics towards high-value branded and innovative pharmaceutical products, biosimilars and biotechnology.
Identifying opportunities in space, aerospace, aircraft components, maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO), defence, electronics, artificial intelligence, quantum computing and machine learning, he called for developing precision engineering and tooling capabilities, establishing advanced testing facilities and partnering with leading global institutions in science, technology and manufacturing.
He also proposed stronger linkages between industry, academia and government to advance research and development and skilling, helping prepare the workforce for future industrial and technological requirements.
Finally, Shri Goyal suggested accelerating ease-of-doing-business reforms through the decriminalisation of minor offences, reduced compliance burdens, simplified procedures and time-bound single-window clearances. Referring to the Centre’s efforts in this direction, he encouraged Telangana to consider similar measures to simplify business operations and citizens’ lives, thereby strengthening ease of living across the State.
Concluding his address, Shri Goyal invoked the symbolism of Diwali, saying that light spreads one diya at a time. He said every investment, export, new job and startup would bring Telangana and the whole nation closer to the shared vision of a developed and prosperous nation by 2047. Inviting investors from India and across the world to explore Telangana’s opportunities, he called for enduring partnerships that generate employment and contribute to the prosperity of the people of Telangana and India.

title: Commerce and Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal Calls for Quality, Scale and Global Market Access to Drive India’s Industrial Transformation
subtitle:
Comprehensive Trade Agreements to Strengthen India’s Global Integration While Safeguarding National Interests: Shri Goyal

Global Demand for Indian Talent Growing, Outlines India’s Clean Energy Goals: Shri Goyal

Shri Goyal Calls for Industry-Academia Collaboration to Drive Innovation and Strengthen Domestic Manufacturing

Startup, Semiconductor and Space Sector to be Growth Drivers of India’s Industrial Transformation: Shri Goyal
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 OCT 2026 3:55PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal has said that India’s industrial transformation must be driven by quality, economies of scale, global market access and inclusivity, with innovation emerging from collaboration among the government, private sector and academia. Addressing the Fourth National Conference on India’s Industrial Transformation, organised by the ISID and IDRA, Minister said that India must aim to become a globally recognised manufacturing nation.
Shri Goyal identified quality, global market access, economies of scale and inclusivity as four key differentiators that could accelerate the transformation of India’s industrial landscape. He said that quality was the most important priority, reiterating Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s emphasis on “Zero Defect, Zero Effect”. With markets opening across the world through free trade agreements, India must compete for market share, expand its global presence and leverage preferential market access. The scale of India’s domestic market of 1.4 billion people, combined with access to international markets, could enable manufacturers to achieve affordability and competitive production costs. He added that sustainable and inclusive growth to ensure wider prosperity for all Indians.
Shri Goyal said that the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 was a collective commitment of 1.4 billion Indians and called for coordinated efforts across government, industry, academia and research institutions to achieve this objective. He said that the country must draw lessons from its economic history, assess its present position realistically and develop an agenda for the future. Emphasising the importance of intergenerational collaboration, he observed that the experience of senior professionals and the energy of young people must come together to address contemporary challenges, rather than working in silos.
On India’s trade policy, Shri Goyal said that the country’s trade agreements were not limited to reducing tariffs, framing rules of origin or securing market access. They were comprehensive partnerships that considered India’s competitive strengths, identified opportunities for exports, protected sensitive sectors and facilitated access to high-technology products, graphics processing units (GPUs), memory technology, medical technology and other goods required for India’s development.
He said that India’s trade negotiations also encompassed services, investments, education, skill development, technology partnerships and cooperation towards climate goals and countries’ intended nationally determined contributions. These comprehensive agreements were laying the foundation for India’s integration with the global economy while protecting its sensitivities and defensive interests through extensive stakeholder consultations before an agreement was concluded.
Referring to the India-US trade deal negotiations, Shri Goyal expressed confidence that when the details of the deal are released, the people of India will recognise that the sensitive interests of farmers and other stakeholders have not been compromised and that India will be placed at a strong comparative advantage.
Shri Goyal explained that trade was fundamentally about comparative advantage and competitiveness, rather than absolute numbers alone. He observed that many developed countries had structured their tariff schedules to impose high duties on labour-intensive goods, using them as negotiating instruments.
He said that India’s trade agreements covered 38 developed and relatively prosperous countries, creating complementary trade opportunities for both sides, with India exporting products they needed and importing products required for its development. He described these as win-win partnerships and emphasised that effective agreements should be fair, equitable and balanced.
Shri Goyal stated that the nine free trade and bilateral trade agreements concluded by the Government had opened up preferential market opportunities in economies with an aggregate GDP of USD 60 trillion, compared with USD 10 trillion covered by agreements concluded before 2014. He said that the earlier agreements were largely with countries competing with India, whereas the current approach sought to foster complementary economic relationships.
He also highlighted the growing international recognition of Indian talent and skills. Recalling a conversation with the German Foreign Minister regarding the migration agreement between India and Germany and the requirement for 90,000 Indians annually, Shri Goyal said that he was told Germany needed substantially more Indian talent. He cited the presence of Indian professionals in senior positions at Fortune 500 companies and among developers of cutting-edge technologies as evidence of the capabilities of India’s workforce.
The Minister expressed confidence that India would continue to be the world’s fastest-growing major economy for another 20 to 25 years, attributing this prospect to the talent, skills and energy of its people.
Shri Goyal stressed that climate action must be guided by the principles of polluter pays and common but differentiated responsibilities, with adequate financial and technological support for developing countries. He highlighted that 60 per cent of India’s installed electricity capacity came from green and renewable sources, while coal remained essential for energy security and affordable power.
Shri Goyal highlighted that India has moved from being predominantly a buyer of products manufactured elsewhere to becoming a country increasingly recognised for manufacturing. The Minister added that the Make in India initiative and phased manufacturing programmes across different sectors had helped bring factories to India and increase domestic production. He said that India would continue to manufacture a growing share of its requirements domestically.
Shri Goyal emphasised that innovation would be central to industrial transformation. Public institutions, private enterprises and academia would need to work together, with the government acting primarily as a facilitator and catalyst for private-sector-led innovation. He highlighted the scientific knowledge, discoveries and research capabilities available in IITs, engineering colleges and other institutions of higher learning and science.
Citing the Startup Fund of Funds, he said that the first fund had been fully utilised and that the second fund was now in place. He also referred to the Research, Development and Innovation Fund (RDIF) in India and said that these initiatives had contributed to the development of India’s startup ecosystem, making it the world’s third-largest.
Shri Goyal also highlighted the opening of the space sector to private participation. He said that India’s space economy, valued at USD 8.4 billion at the time of his address, had the potential to reach USD 44 billion by 2033. He observed that international partners were increasingly interested in collaboration with India in space, artificial intelligence, computing and startups.
Referring to his recent visit to Germany, Shri Goyal said that German research institutions, some employing twelve to thirty thousand people, were working closely with the private sector and have expressed interest in collaborating with India. He attributed this growing interest to the trust in partnership between India and Germany and to the confidence that India offered in terms of talent, skills, fair play and equal opportunity.
The Minister said that the new trade agreements and international relationships being developed under Prime Minister Modi’s leadership were opening opportunities for joint research, technology development and industrial collaboration. He said that these partnerships could help India transform its growth trajectory by combining domestic capabilities with international expertise and investment.
Shri Goyal concluded by commending ISID for organising three days of serious deliberations on India’s industrial future. He reiterated that the country’s industrial transformation would depend on sustained attention to quality, access to global markets, economies of scale and inclusivity, supported by collaboration across manufacturing, innovation and research. He extended his best wishes to the conference and its participants for their contributions towards achieving Viksit Bharat 2047.

date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 OCT 2026 5:45PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In furtherance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of ‘Sahkar se Samriddhi’ and towards accelerating cooperative-led development that reaches every citizen and includes every section of society, the 93rd Meeting of the General Council of the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC) was held today at the Corporation's headquarters in New Delhi under the chairmanship of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah. The meeting deliberated on various matters relating to NCDC's financial and institutional achievements, expansion of financing in the cooperative sector, development of new Multi-State Cooperative Societies, strengthening of rural livelihoods and the Corporation's future roadmap.
Addressing the General Council meeting, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that NCDC has delivered highly commendable performance over the past nearly five years. The Corporation has not only made significant progress in its financial performance and achievement of prescribed targets but has also recorded important accomplishments, including increased profit per employee, expansion in loan sanctions and disbursements, and maintenance of zero net Non-Performing Assets (NPAs). He expressed particular satisfaction that NCDC has now established its presence in all States and Union Territories of the country. The expansion of offices into remote regions such as Ladakh and smaller States of the North-East marks an important step towards taking the cooperative movement to the remotest parts of the country. Shri Amit Shah congratulated the officers and employees of the Corporation on these achievements.
Shri Amit Shah said that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi fulfilled a decades-old demand of the cooperative sector by establishing a separate Ministry of Cooperation. The objective is not merely to increase the number of cooperative institutions but to connect every citizen of the country with the development process. He observed that the development of a vast country like India cannot be assessed solely on the basis of Gross Domestic Product, per capita income or industrial investment. True development also means ensuring that every section of society has access to opportunities, every citizen can lead a life of dignity and everyone is able to contribute to the nation's progress. He explained that development reaching every citizen signifies Sarvasparshi Vikas, while Sarvasamaveshi Vikas means ensuring equal participation of all regions, from Ladakh to Lakshadweep, in the country's development journey.
The Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that cooperation is the most effective means of connecting the collective strength of small farmers, livestock rearers, rural women, fishermen and economically weaker sections, who have limited capital, with national development. Cooperative institutions can bring together large numbers of people with limited capital and create new opportunities in production, processing, marketing and income generation. He said that Amul, IFFCO and several other successful cooperative institutions in the country demonstrate that globally competitive organisations can be developed by combining cooperative values with professional management. Referring to the outstanding performance of Indian cooperative institutions in international cooperative rankings, he described it as a matter of pride for the entire cooperative sector of the country.
Shri Amit Shah said that NCDC has expanded its activities across production, processing, marketing, rural industrial activities, water conservation, agricultural insurance, cooperative banking and sectors associated with the circular economy. The Corporation has also played a significant role in the formation, capital investment and operations of national-level Multi-State Cooperative Societies. He observed that, considering NCDC's achievements over the past five years, this period could be described as a golden era of sorts for the Corporation. However, he emphasised that these achievements should not lead to complacency. Comprehensive reforms are needed in the Corporation's institutional structure, capacity to mobilise financial resources, professional functioning and models of partnership with cooperative institutions to meet changing requirements.
The Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation directed NCDC to prepare a comprehensive roadmap for the next 25 years. He said that a group comprising experienced representatives of the cooperative sector and professional experts should be constituted to examine the Corporation's existing structure, alternative avenues for capital mobilisation, participation of cooperative institutions, financial autonomy, organisational reforms and future business opportunities. He also suggested organising a workshop on these issues. Shri Amit Shah said that a special meeting should be convened for detailed presentations and deliberations on the subject so that progress could be made towards taking the necessary decisions.
Shri Amit Shah said that the administrative systems of cooperative institutions should be professional, while their fundamental approach must remain rooted in cooperative principles. He observed that excessive dependence on government assistance and government banks creates certain limitations for institutional development. NCDC should, therefore, develop financial and organisational models that enable the Corporation to mobilise resources in line with its growing requirements and fully harness the potential of the cooperative sector. He said that while the development of the cooperative sector is NCDC's responsibility, ensuring NCDC's own development should be the collective resolve of all members of the General Council.
The Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation appreciated NCDC's role in the development of institutions such as National Cooperative Exports Limited (NCEL), Bharatiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited (BBSSL), National Cooperative Organics Limited (NCOL), Bharat Taxi, Sahakar Sarathi and the National Urban Cooperative Finance and Development Corporation (NUCFDC), the umbrella organisation for Urban Cooperative Banks. He expressed confidence that these institutions could emerge as large and influential Multi-State Cooperative Societies at the national level in the coming years. He said that, alongside providing financial assistance to large cooperative enterprises, bringing about direct improvements in the livelihoods of small farmers, livestock rearers and fishermen is an equally important responsibility of NCDC.
Citing an example from the fisheries sector, Shri Amit Shah said that financial assistance has been sanctioned through NCDC for approximately 100 trawlers engaged in deep-sea fishing. Highlighting the social and economic impact of this initiative, he observed that such financing has the potential to significantly increase the monthly incomes of a large number of fishing families. He said that although a project of this scale may appear relatively small to a major financial institution, the transformation it can bring to the lives of the families concerned, their children's education and their future opportunities is extremely significant. He encouraged the Corporation to further expand such grassroots initiatives.
Shri Amit Shah also emphasised the need to develop new business models based on the circular economy for cooperative sugar mills. Referring to proposed new Multi-State cooperative initiatives in Kolhapur and Pune in Maharashtra, he said that common processing and industrial facilities could be developed for ethanol, CNG, chemicals and other value-added products associated with sugar mills. This would particularly benefit cooperative sugar mills that are not in a position to make large investments or establish modern processing plants independently. Emphasis was also placed on ensuring that the benefits generated through such arrangements reach the cooperative sugar mills concerned.
Emphasising greater participation of youth, the Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that qualified young people who have completed training and internships under the ‘Sahakar Mitra’ programme should be associated with new Multi-State Cooperative Societies. This would promote modern management practices, business efficiency and professional leadership in cooperative institutions. Referring to the study of Banas Dairy's successful management model, he suggested drawing upon its experiences to strengthen NCDC's future operations and institutional development.
Shri Amit Shah stressed the need to rapidly increase NCDC's financial disbursements in the coming years. Referring to the targets of ₹1.70 lakh crore for FY 2026–27, ₹2.10 lakh crore for FY 2027–28 and ₹2.50 lakh crore for FY 2028–29, he called for setting even more ambitious targets for subsequent years. He emphasised working towards disbursements of approximately ₹3.50 lakh crore in FY 2029–30 and ₹4 lakh crore in FY 2030–31. Shri Amit Shah said that, given the growing opportunities in dairy, fisheries, cooperative banking and other sectors, NCDC must enhance its financial capacity proportionately so that the financing requirements of the cooperative sector can be met through a cooperative-based institutional framework.
The Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation appreciated the support extended by the Reserve Bank of India and the Ministry of Finance towards NCDC's development. He said that positive cooperation has been received at various levels to address the Corporation's financial and regulatory challenges, and efforts would continue to remove the remaining obstacles. He suggested that NCDC explore opportunities for developing consortium and co-financing models in collaboration with NABARD, State Cooperative Banks and commercial banks. He also emphasised developing new financing models to meet the entire financial requirements of the dairy cooperative sector.
Giving special priority to the development of the North-Eastern Region, Shri Amit Shah said that a target has been set to make the North-East self-reliant in the production of milk, eggs, fish and meat by 2030. He observed that a substantial portion of the region's current requirements in these sectors is met from outside the region, despite the immense potential for dairy, fisheries and animal husbandry in the North-East. He said that achieving self-reliance in these four sectors could lead to an unprecedented increase in the region's income and generate employment opportunities. He directed NCDC's offices in the North-East to prepare practical projects focused on these sectors, provide the necessary financing and implement them in collaboration with the respective State Governments.
According to the financial details presented during the meeting, NCDC has cumulatively disbursed financial assistance amounting to ₹4,14,586 crore to cooperative institutions across the country from the establishment of the Ministry of Cooperation up to 25 October 2026. During FY 2025–26, the Corporation sanctioned projects worth ₹1,55,408 crore and disbursed financial assistance of ₹1,27,596 crore. During the same period, the Corporation earned a net profit of ₹1,475 crore, while its loan recovery rate stood at 99.84 per cent and net NPA remained zero. NCDC's annual disbursements increased from ₹24,733 crore in FY 2020–21 to ₹1,27,596 crore in FY 2025–26, representing an approximately fivefold increase over the past five years. The 3,339 units and projects sanctioned by NCDC during FY 2025–26 provided for benefits to 14,881 cooperative societies.
The meeting also discussed the significance of the National Cooperative Development Corporation (Amendment) Act, 2026. Passed by both Houses of Parliament and having received the assent of the President, the Act was published in the Gazette of India on 14 August 2026. The amendment has expanded the avenues for providing financial assistance for cooperative development, institutional participation and new investment opportunities through equity and share capital. With the objective of making financial assistance more accessible and competitive for cooperative institutions, the Central Government has approved grant assistance of ₹2,000 crore for NCDC, enabling the Corporation to make arrangements to mobilise ₹20,000 crore from the market over four years. Under this initiative, loans amounting to ₹9,380 crore were disbursed during FY 2025–26 and ₹6,172 crore during FY 2026–27 up to 25 October.
To promote innovation and entrepreneurship in the cooperative sector, NCDC has launched the ‘Sahakar Navachar Yojana’. The scheme provides for 100 per cent grant assistance of up to ₹25 lakh to eligible cooperative institutions. An initial corpus of ₹10 crore has been established for the scheme, with 20 per cent of the funds earmarked for cooperative institutions in the North-Eastern Region, hilly areas and disadvantaged sections. So far, grant assistance totalling ₹85 lakh has been sanctioned to five cooperative institutions. In addition, cooperative institutions are being provided guidance and support in business development, digital accounting, financial management, branding and market linkages.
To promote human resource development and capacity building in cooperative institutions, NCDC's Laxmanrao Inamdar National Academy for Cooperative Research and Development (LINAC) and its regional training centres are conducting extensive training programmes. During FY 2025–26, a total of 21,688 participants attended 227 training programmes. The agreement between NCDC and Tribhuvan Sahkari University (TSU) to enhance modern management, digital technology, financial discipline, branding and professional competence in cooperative institutions is a commendable step.
The General Council meeting also reviewed the audited annual accounts, annual report and financial performance for FY 2025–26, besides deliberating on financial programmes for the coming years, opportunities for resource mobilisation and the growing financing requirements of the cooperative sector. Special emphasis was placed on the Corporation's long-term strategy in the context of the financial proposals included in the meeting's agenda and the ambitious future disbursement targets suggested by the Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation during his address.
Concluding his address, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah congratulated NCDC's officers, members of the General Council and employees on the Corporation's financial performance, zero net NPA and institutional expansion. He expressed confidence that NCDC would continue to expand its scope of activities, financial capacity and professional functioning, and play an important role in realising Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of ‘Sahkar se Samriddhi’, making cooperation a powerful instrument of rural prosperity, employment generation, economic self-reliance and inclusive national development.

Addressing the 13th ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting (ADMM) - Plus in Cebu, Philippines on October 29, 2026, he asserted that every strategy of India has been tested, refined, and proven in the crucible of real-world operations. He added that this proactive, battle-tested doctrine was decisively demonstrated during Operation Sindoor, when India dismantled terrorist infrastructure and enforced a non-negotiable red line against state-sponsored terror.
Raksha Mantri underlined that terrorism knows no borders and India stands fully prepared to share its practical, battle-tested experience with ADMM-Plus partners through joint exercises, capacity-building programmes, and robust intelligence sharing to strengthen collective capabilities. He stressed that counter-terrorism remains an important area of cooperation under the ADMM-Plus framework, and India & Malaysia are co-chairing the Experts’ Working Group on Counter-Terrorism for the 2024 to 2027 cycle.
Shri Rajnath Singh reiterated that India attaches importance to ASEAN centrality and a secure, open, inclusive, resilient and rule-based Indo-Pacific, where peace & stability are not just aspirations but a result of collective commitment. He stated that its strategic engagement with ASEAN is long-term and rooted in shared interests, mutual respect and practical cooperation. He recalled that the second ASEAN-India Defence Ministers’ Informal Meeting in Kuala Lumpur in October last year reaffirmed the commitment to advancing the defence and security components of the ASEAN-India Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and the ASEAN-India Plan of Action for 2026 to 2030.
On the theme of 13th ADMM-Plus
‘Navigating Our Future, Together’
, Raksha Mantri stated that it resonates with India’s foreign and defence policy paradigms as well as its civilisational ethos of ‘
Sarve Bhavantu Sukhinah’
(May all beings be happy) that reflects the aspiration for the happiness, prosperity, and well-being of all the people across the world. “This theme reminds us that our greatest strength lies in our solidarity and the shared ability to leverage our geographic, economic and strategic diversity. India believes in an international system built on mutual trust, co-operation, and collective responsibility. It is this precise collaborative spirit that empowers us to overcome the challenges to peace and order,” he said.
Shri Rajnath Singh described maritime cooperation as crucial to India’s engagement with ASEAN during 2026, highlighting New Delhi’s designation of 2026 as the ASEAN-India Year of Maritime Cooperation and the conduct of the second ASEAN-India Maritime Exercise. He emphasised that India does not merely preach the tenets of international maritime law; it is a steadfast practitioner of global laws concerning maritime security. “Our commitment to ensuring the freedom of navigation and safeguarding global Sea Lines of Communication is backed by a continuous, decades-long operational legacy. Since 2008, the Indian Navy has maintained an uninterrupted, active presence in highly volatile corridors like the Gulf of Aden, without coercion or unilateral actions that undermine the rights of other nations,” he said.
Raksha Mantri highlighted that by deploying frontline warships, India has successfully escorted thousands of merchant vessels and thwarted dozens of high-seas hijackings, extending protection to commercial shipping irrespective of flag or nationality. He termed the security of commercial shipping as India’s responsibility. “In an era where global trade routes face complex transnational threats, India stands ready to move beyond rhetoric. There is a need for effective action, regular operational presence and international cooperation. India will continue serving as a reliable net security provider in the Indian Ocean Region and the wider Indo-Pacific,” he said.
Underlining that maritime security is closely connected with the safety and prosperity of the wider region, Shri Rajnath Singh said India’s emphasis on the rule of law, particularly the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, and its advocacy for freedom of navigation and overflight are not directed against any country but are meant to safeguard the collective interests of all regional stakeholders who depend on open sea lanes and stable maritime governance. He stated that India gives due respect to maritime safety, search & rescue, humanitarian assistance, professional interaction, capacity building and international law, and India remains ready to work with ASEAN partners in strengthening cooperation in these areas.
Raksha Mantri highlighted the importance of youth engagement in strengthening India-ASEAN defence cooperation, stating that the shared demographic profile and aspirations of the young populations provide a strong foundation for deeper regional partnership. He proposed the establishment of a dedicated defence ‘Youth Bridge’ to enhance institutional people-to-people connectivity, promote digital innovation and facilitate capacity building in line with ADMM-Plus initiatives. He stated that empowering youth and providing them with greater opportunities to contribute to regional peace and security is consistent with the theme of ‘Youth, Peace and Security’ and is essential for building a peaceful, resilient and prosperous Indo-Pacific.

title: Clarification on the Process of Strategic Restructuring of the IDBI Bank Ltd.
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 OCT 2026 9:54PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The first or initial bid round was conducted in the financial year 2025-26 by DIPAM as per its internal practices, which are in the nature of indicative guidelines and not hidebound rules or regulations. The foreword itself states that the procedure suggested is not to be construed as a rigid, legal framework, which may require due adaptation/ modification in the best interest of successful execution of the transaction in a time bound manner. Given the complex nature of strategic transactions, the indicative guidelines give flexibility to ensure cost and time spent in lengthy processes is not wasted.
The press note dated 14.10.2026 clearly explains that there is no
a-priori
benchmark for bidding. The bidders do their own valuation and submit their bids in a confidential manner. Independent agencies are hired to do a fair valuation of the enterprise contemporaneously, which is then used as a comparator to assess the reasonableness of the bids submitted. The bid discovered price and the comparative valuation can, therefore, be above or below each other.
To handle this situation, provision is
ex-ante
built into Para 5.3.6(iii) the RFP:
“In the event the Financial Bid of the Highest Bidder is lower than the reserve price, the Gol will decide the further course of action and the QIPs shall not subsequently question any decision taken by the Gol in this regard.”
There is no procedure prescribed to handle this situation internally within DIPAM and special powers have been delegated to the Core Group of Secretaries on Disinvestment (CGD) by the Cabinet Committee of Economic Affairs (CCEA) for this purpose. In its meeting dated August 16, 2017, while approving the Note titled ‘Procedure and Mechanism for Strategic Disinvestment - Delegation Thereof’, the CCEA has empowered the CGD to remove all difficulties, including deviations from procedure, to ensure effective implementation of the strategic disinvestment transactions approved by the CCEA. The abstract of the decision is as follows:
“8.1 Approval of the CCEA is solicited in case of strategic disinvestment...(ii) for empowering the CGD to take policy decisions with regard to procedural issues and to consider deviations as necessary from time to time for (the) effective implementation of decisions of CCEA”. Decision: Approved in the CCEA Meeting dated August 16th, 2017.
In due exercise of these powers, the procedure for the second or the best offer round was determined by the CGD itself. The reserve price was neither decreased, nor increased, and the first round itself became functus officio after the initial bids were not approved.
The entire valuation methodology was reviewed by the CGD in April, 2026 before the invitation of best offer bids.  Since the comparator used for valuation has to be contemporaneous with the bids received, and 31st March, 2026 closing financial accounts were released in the public domain in end-April, the independent valuation agencies had started working on the revised valuations in May, 2026 itself. The process remained double blind because the bidder did not know the valuation and the valuators did not see the bids. It is only the CGD which gets to see a complete picture and compares the bids with fair valuations to take a final call on the reasonableness of the bids submitted.
The valuation was carried out by two different advisers, independent of each other, using independent and distinct methodologies. The Business Valuation is always done through the Transaction Adviser as per the protocol, who, given the complex nature of this transaction, further appointed professional experts trained in the Market Multiple Method. To explain briefly, the Market Multiple method is of two sub-types: the Comparable Company Method and the Comparable Transaction Method. Since suitable comparable transaction were not available, comparable companies’ method was used, which in this case were all the listed public sector banks. It is pertinent to mention here that the IDBI was a government ‘owned’ banking company till 2019, but became a government ‘controlled’ banking company after the LIC acquired majority stakes in 2019. Since there is no specific regulatory protocol for this situation, the RBI started treating it as a private bank only for regulatory purposes, even though the ownership stayed overwhelmingly with the LIC and the GoI, and the market investors continued to value it as a public sector entity.
The Asset Valuer also used robust and time-tested methodologies, including additional value for disputed tax demands, which were indemnified as a common demand of the qualified bidders to nudge the bid offer upwards. This remains a low probability event and revenue neutral for the government, as only the additional tax demand, if paid at all, will be eligible for reimbursement. The potential liability that could arise on this account was only Rs. 627 crores while the bid discovered price increased by Rs 3,917 crores enhancing the value of the transaction for the GoI and the LIC.
The details of the volatile stock price of the narrowly traded IDBI stock and why it was discarded are well explained in the press note date 14.10.2026. The GoI and the LIC retain residual shareholdings to get further benefit from the upside that is expected from the value enhancement following strategic restructuring of the IDBI Bank going forward in future.

Energy conservation measures, including optimised air-conditioning and switching off equipment when not required, have resulted in a reported reduction of 7.68 lakh kWh in electricity consumption, a decline of 10.5 per cent. To promote sustainable mobility, AIIMS operates 40 free in-campus electric vehicle shuttle services for patients and attendants. The campus also has 30 EV chargers and 114 dedicated power points across four locations, supported by smart monitoring systems.

The visit reaffirmed the importance of sustained cleanliness initiatives, effective waste management and improved patient amenities in public healthcare institutions. Through Special Campaign 6, the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare continues to emphasise that cleanliness must be institutionalised as an ongoing practice, supported by efficient management, collective responsibility and a patient-centric approach to healthcare delivery.

title: Advancing Universal and Inclusive Senior Care: Ayushman Vay Vandana Marks Two Years of Transforming Healthcare for Elderly Citizens
subtitle:
6 Crore Senior Citizens Aged 70 Years and Above Empowered with Dignified, Cashless Healthcare Coverage, Irrespective of Socio-Economic Status

Ayushman Vay Vandana Provided 23.46 Lakh Hospital Admissions Valued at ₹5,668.80 Crore in Two Years

From Cataract Surgery to Cardiac Care: Ayushman Vay Vandana Facilitates Access to Cashless Hospital Treatment for Senior Citizens Aged 70 Years and Above 

Transforming Senior Cardiac Care: Over ₹649 Crore Sanctioned for Advanced Heart Interventions
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 OCT 2026 3:33PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Driven by the continuous efforts and relentless dedication of the Government of India towards building an inclusive, accessible and world-class healthcare system, Ayushman Vay Vandana has successfully completed two years today. Launched by the Hon’ble Prime Minister on 29th October 2024, this transformative initiative extends the benefits of the landmark Ayushman Bharat- Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY) to every citizen aged 70 years and above, irrespective of their socio-economic status.
Implemented by the National Health Authority (NHA) under the aegis of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, the initiative marks an important step towards extending health coverage and strengthening financial protection for approximately 6 crore senior citizens, belonging to around 4.5 crore families, across the country.
Under Ayushman Vay Vandana, all senior citizens aged 70 years and above are eligible for health coverage of up to ₹5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalisation.
For senior citizens aged 70 years and above, belonging to families already covered under AB PM-JAY, an additional top-up cover of up to ₹5 lakh per year is available exclusively for themselves, separate from the cover available to other family members below 70 years of age. This provision extends the scheme’s financial protection to eligible senior citizens aged 70 years and above, while preserving the coverage available to other family members.
As on 20 October 2026, the initiative has recorded
23.46 lakh authorised hospital admissions
, reflecting the utilisation of hospital services by eligible senior citizens aged 70 years and above, under the scheme. The total value of these admissions stands at
₹5,668.80 crore
, representing the value of hospital care authorised under the scheme.
Cataract surgery is the most frequently availed procedure, with 4.71 lakh treatments constituting approximately 20.1 per cent of all authorised treatments. The volume of these procedures indicates that the initiative is addressing a long-standing gap in access to eye care among the elderly.
Chronic haemodialysis ranks next, with approximately 2.90 lakh treatments, providing sustained support to beneficiaries who require regular hospital-based care for kidney disease.
In terms of authorised value,
Percutaneous Transluminal Coronary Angioplasty (PTCA) accounts for the largest share, at approximately ₹649 crore
. This underlines the role of the initiative in safeguarding beneficiaries against the high cost of specialised cardiac care.
Other prominent treatment categories include total knee replacement, management of acute exacerbation of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), acute febrile illness, and acute kidney injury and renal failure. Taken together, these procedures span the continuum of hospital care, from routine surgical interventions to the management of complex and critical conditions.
Speaking on the occasion, Dr. Sunil Kumar Barnwal, CEO, National Health Authority, said, “Ayushman Vay Vandana embodies our commitment to ensuring that senior citizens aged 70 years and above, can access healthcare with dignity, security and peace of mind. By extending AB PM-JAY coverage to all eligible citizens aged 70 years and above, irrespective of socio-economic status, the initiative strengthens financial protection for the elderly families. It is an important step towards building a more inclusive healthcare system that recognises the needs of our senior citizens and ensures that financial constraints do not stand in the way of essential hospital care.”
By extending the benefits of AB PM-JAY to all eligible senior citizens, irrespective of socio-economic status, Ayushman Vay Vandana reinforces the commitment of the Government of India to inclusive healthcare and financial protection in old age. As the initiative enters its third year, it will continue to widen the reach of publicly funded health coverage and to reduce the financial burden of hospitalisation on senior citizens and their families.

title: From Bharat to Antalya: Delhi Declaration 2026 Calls for Stronger Multilevel Climate Action Ahead of COP31
subtitle:
Second edition of two-day ARISE Cities Forum closes with a collective call for greater role of cities in global climate governance.

Theme of the forum addresses timely and urgent concerns, says Turkish Ambassador
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 OCT 2026 3:14PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The ARISE Cities Forum 2026 concluded in New Delhi with the adoption of the
Delhi Declaration on Local Action for Global Climate Goals
on 28 October 2026. Held on 27-28 October 2026 at the India Habitat Centre, the second edition of the Forum was organised by ICLEI South Asia, in collaboration with the National Institute of Urban Affairs (NIUA), with support from the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, Government of India.
The Forum brought together more th
an 200 participants from 50+ citi
es across 18+ countries to bring urban voices from across the Global South to the forefront, emphasising the values of collaboration, sustainability, resilience, and equity in driving climate action through measurable, locally driven initiatives. The two-day Forum comprised three technical plenaries and 14 technical sessions.
Themed
“From Bharat to Antalya — Commit. Implement. Deliver,”
the Forum made a united call by cities and local governments across the Global South for stronger multilevel collaboration and recognition as indispensable partners in global climate governance. This collective ambition, articulated in the Delhi Declaration 2026, will now travel to COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye.
From commitment to implementation: Highlights from the Closing Ceremony
The Forum closed on 28 October 2026 with addresses by
H.E. Ali Murat Ersoy
, Ambassador of the Republic of Türkiye to India;
Pravesh Wahi
, Hon’ble Mayor of Delhi;
Mikiko Tanaka
, Head of Subregional Office for South and South-West Asia, UNESCAP;
Dr Vinay P. Sahasrabuddhe
, State In-Charge for the Bharatiya Janata Party in Delhi; President, Asiatic Society of Mumbai;
Dr Debolina Kundu
, Director, National Institute of Urban Affairs; and
Gino Van Begin
, Secretary General, ICLEI.
Samed Ağırbaş
, COP31 Climate Champion and President of the Zero Waste Foundation, joined virtually for a special address.
H.E. Ali Murat Ersoy, Ambassador of the Republic of Türkiye to India
, “On behalf of the Republic of Turkey, as we prepare to host COP21 in Antalya, I extend our deepest appreciation to ICLEI South Asia, NIUA and UN Habitat for convening with the ARISE Cities Forum 2026. The journey from ‘Bharat to Antalya’ should be a continuum of action. Turkey's host priorities align seamlessly with the Indian approach to climate action, an approach anchored in the timeless philosophy of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, ‘the world is one family’.
Pravesh Wahi, Hon’ble Mayor of Delhi
said, “ICLEI South Asia has supported Delhi in promoting public transport, expanding the electric bus fleet, and improving last-mile connectivity, working with municipal corporations in Delhi and the National Capital Region to build city leadership, raise awareness, and implement pilot interventions to improve air quality. I commend and thank ICLEI South Asia for this work.”
Mikiko Tanaka, Head of Subregional Office for South and South-West Asia, UNESCAP
, “I wish to support the Delhi Declaration with messages from a recent ESCAP regional discussion paper that underlines the importance of localizing NDCs to cities.Cities must move to the centre of national climate action. They should close the gap between national commitment and implementation. Mayors need to sit at the table where national climate commitments are made. Climate finance must reach cities, and cities must be ready to use it. Climate action must not happen in sectoral silos. National climate commitments must translate into local climate action plans. South-South cooperation can help cities accelerate climate action.”
Dr. Vinay P. Sahasrabuddhe, State In-Charge for the Bharatiya Janata Party in Delhi; President, Asiatic Society of Mumbai
said
“
The concept of a dormitory city now dominates the discourse around urban administration. In this situation, people do not feel connected to the city where they work, even though it is their workplace. A sense of belonging is therefore important for sustainable urban administration. Cities are not just clusters of buildings, gated communities, and skyscrapers. Cities, after all, are living organisms. For cities to become vibrant centers of sharing and caring, some kind of emotional connection is essential. I therefore urge lawmakers and urban administrators to look into this.”
Samed Ağırbaş, COP31 Climate Champion, President of the Zero Waste Foundation
, “Local leaders know what their communities need. They must have the finance resources and partnership to act. That is why the Delhi Declaration is so relevant.
I particularly welcome the Delhi Declaration’s commitment to zero waste, because the future of our planet begins in our home.
Let us turn the Declaration into lasting partnership and practical action.”
Dr. Debolina Kundu, Director, National Institute of Urban Affairs, India
“
The ARISE Delhi Declaration 2026: Local Action for Global Climate Goals sets a collective direction for taking the outcomes of the Forum forward to COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye. Its emphasis on integrated local action, a just clean energy transition, accessible finance and meaningful community participation reflects the priorities that have brought us together.”
Gino Van Begin, Secretary General, ICLEI – Local Governments for Sustainability
“The ARISE Cities Forum 2026 explored the role of multi-level governance and the cooperation required among all levels of government in the Paris Agreement countries to achieve the Agreement’s targets, at both the national and local levels. We discussed the priorities that need to be set for sub-national planning across sectors, from urban heat to water stress, infrastructure, and mobility. We discussed the need for investment and for rapid implementation. We discussed the need to accelerate partnerships and make them inclusive for climate-resilient development. We also reinforced our shared urban climate resolve by adopting the Delhi Declaration of the ARISE Cities Forum 2026.”
The Closing Ceremony also marked the launch of the Delhi Biodiversity Map developed by ICLEI South Asia.
The ARISE Cities Forum 2026 closed with the adoption of the Delhi Declaration and its formal handover to
Gino Van Begin,
marking a key milestone in carrying the Forum’s collective commitments and urban priorities forward to COP31 in Antalya.
Delhi Declaration 2026: Taking the urban ambitions of the Global South to COP31
Building on the 2025 Declaration, the
Delhi Declaration on Local Action for Global Climate Goals 2026
embodies the spirit of solidarity, partnership, and a whole-of-economy and society approach that must define climate action beyond COP31, offering the commitment of cities of the Global South to co-create a climate-safe, just, and sustainable future for all.
The Declaration positions
cities as key contributors to international climate negotiations
, bringing the experiences and priorities of the Global South into the UNFCCC process. It echoes the Local Government and Municipal Administration (LGMA) Constituency’s push for stronger links between urban development and climate action by setting out
ten shared commitments
:
1. Advance the Global Climate Agenda from Pre-COP31 to COP31
2. Accelerate Adaptation and Synergies Across Conventions
3. Advance Circularity Through Cooperation and Collective Action
4. Achieve an Energy Transition Outcome that recognises and accelerates subnational delivery to return to the 1.5°C pathway
5. Prioritise Ambitious Just Transitions
6. Institutionalise Multilevel Climate Finance
7. Uphold Independent Science and Data Systems
8. Create a Systematic Joint Space for Multilevel Action
9. Champion Global South Climate Urban Leadership
10. Strengthen Youth and Community Leadership in Climate Action
With 2026 marking a pivotal ‘Triple COP’ year, the Delhi Declaration 2026 takes on added significance as a call for
coordinated action across the climate, biodiversity and land agendas
, recognising the interconnected challenges cities face.
As the global climate community prepares for COP31, the Delhi Declaration adopted at the ARISE Cities Forum 2026 reinforces the message that global climate goals can only be achieved when local priorities, resources and implementation capacities are integrated into climate decision-making.
For more information on the ARISE Cities Forum 2026 and its agenda, please visit:
https://arisecitiesforum.org/
